# File paths for source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_2.csv"

source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_4.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2016']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2014']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', '(Fall 2000)', ..., '(Fall 2014)']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2015']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

# Step 1: Rename columns in df0, df1, df3 to match target columns
# year 2014 -> persist 2014 (int)
# year 2015 -> persist 2015 (int)
# year 2016 -> persist 2016 (int)
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"year 2016": "persist 2016"})
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={"year 2014": "persist 2014"})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={"year 2015": "persist 2015"})

# Step 2: Select only needed columns from df2 for target:
# Target needs (Fall 2011), (Fall 2012), (Fall 2013), (Fall 2014)
df2_selected = df2[["Institution", "(Fall 2011)", "(Fall 2012)", "(Fall 2013)", "(Fall 2014)"]]

# Step 3: df4 already has ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']
# Just ensure types are correct (Cohort columns as int)
df4_selected = df4.copy()

# Step 4: Merge all dataframes on 'Institution'
# Start merging from df2_selected (which has the largest set of columns for the target)
# Merge order: df2_selected + df1_renamed + df3_renamed + df0_renamed + df4_selected

# Merge df2 and df1 (persist 2014)
df_merge_1 = pd.merge(df2_selected, df1_renamed, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Merge with df3 (persist 2015)
df_merge_2 = pd.merge(df_merge_1, df3_renamed, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Merge with df0 (persist 2016)
df_merge_3 = pd.merge(df_merge_2, df0_renamed, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Merge with df4 (Cohort columns)
df_final = pd.merge(df_merge_3, df4_selected, on="Institution", how="outer")

# Step 5: Ensure correct column order as per target schema
target_columns = [
    "Institution",
    "(Fall 2011)",
    "(Fall 2012)",
    "(Fall 2013)",
    "(Fall 2014)",
    "persist 2014",
    "persist 2015",
    "persist 2016",
    "Cohort 2014",
    "Cohort 2015",
    "Cohort 2016",
]

# Some columns might be missing due to outer join, fill them with NaN or appropriate type
for col in target_columns:
    if col not in df_final.columns:
        # Add missing columns with NaN
        df_final[col] = pd.NA

# Reorder columns
df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Step 6: Convert data types to match target schema
# Institution: string
df_final["Institution"] = df_final["Institution"].astype(str)

# (Fall xxxx): float
for col in ["(Fall 2011)", "(Fall 2012)", "(Fall 2013)", "(Fall 2014)"]:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce')

# persist xxxx: integer (some may have NaN, convert carefully)
for col in ["persist 2014", "persist 2015", "persist 2016"]:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Cohort xxxx: integer (some may have NaN, convert carefully)
for col in ["Cohort 2014", "Cohort 2015", "Cohort 2016"]:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Step 7: Sort by Institution alphabetically for neatness (optional)
df_final = df_final.sort_values(by="Institution").reset_index(drop=True)

# Step 8: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/target_multisource_cot.csv"

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join the three "year" tables (source0, source1, source3) on 'Institution'
# These tables have schema: ['Institution', 'year XXXX']
# The target columns 'persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016' correspond to these years
# Join on 'Institution' key using inner join to keep only institutions present in all
persist_df = source1.rename(columns={'year 2014': 'persist 2014'}) \
    .merge(source3.rename(columns={'year 2015': 'persist 2015'}), on='Institution', how='inner') \
    .merge(source0.rename(columns={'year 2016': 'persist 2016'}), on='Institution', how='inner')

# Step 2: From source2, select columns for Fall 2011 to Fall 2014 plus Institution
fall_cols = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']
fall_df = source2[fall_cols]

# Step 3: From source4, select 'Institution' and 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016'
# Convert cohort columns to integer type (target expects int)
cohort_cols = ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']
cohort_df = source4[cohort_cols].copy()
cohort_df['Cohort 2014'] = pd.to_numeric(cohort_df['Cohort 2014'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
cohort_df['Cohort 2015'] = pd.to_numeric(cohort_df['Cohort 2015'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
cohort_df['Cohort 2016'] = pd.to_numeric(cohort_df['Cohort 2016'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Step 4: Join fall_df, persist_df, and cohort_df on 'Institution'
# Use inner joins to keep only institutions present in all sources (matches target keys)
merged_df = fall_df.merge(persist_df, on='Institution', how='inner') \
                   .merge(cohort_df, on='Institution', how='inner')

# Step 5: Ensure data types match target schema
# Fall columns are float, persist and cohort columns are Int64 (nullable integer)
for col in ['persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016']:
    merged_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged_df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

for col in ['(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']:
    merged_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged_df[col], errors='coerce')

# Step 6: The target table has unique Institution keys
# GroupBy on 'Institution' to ensure uniqueness (in case of duplicates)
# Since Institution is key, no aggregation needed beyond taking first occurrence
final_df = merged_df.groupby('Institution', as_index=False).first()

# Step 7: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = final_df[['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)',

                     'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']]

# Step 8: Sort by Institution alphabetically for neatness (optional)
final_df = final_df.sort_values(by='Institution').reset_index(drop=True)

# Step 9: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
